outcome: Fetal muscle protein fractional synthesis rate
Isotope enrichments in free amino acids and fetal muscle, liver, and placenta protein
cohort: Pregnant rats were fed either a control (20% protein) or a low-protein (4% protein) diet, with low-protein dams randomly allocated to drink tap water either as such or supplemented with L-citrulline, L-arginine, or nonessential L-amino acids.
finding: L-Citrulline and L-arginine supplementation equally increased fetal weight in a rat model of IUGR induced by maternal dietary protein restriction, and L-citrulline also normalized fetal muscle protein synthesis.
birth_weight: Fetal weights ranged from 3.82 ± 0.06 g (LP group) to 5.41 ± 0.10 g (control group); L-citrulline increased fetal weight to 4.15 ± 0.08 g, and L-arginine to 4.13 ± 0.1 g.
